Reference / fs/directory

fs/directory#

Directory is a narrow path command object.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for DirectoryEntries(origin: Directory(path: root)) -> entry {
    output.writeln(entry.path().string());
}

Description#

Directory is a narrow path command object. create() creates one level with portable 0755 permissions filtered by the process umask. remove() removes only an empty directory and throws FileError.not_empty otherwise.

DirectoryEntries snapshots and lexicographically sorts one directory in one native bulk operation when cursor() is requested:

Descendants performs deterministic preorder traversal. It snapshots only the directory currently being entered, not the complete tree:

for Descendants(origin: Directory(path: root)) -> entry {
    output.writeln(entry.kind().string(), " ", entry.path().string());
}

Directory symlinks are yielded as symbolic_link entries and never followed. DirectoryTree applies the same leaf rule while deleting children bottom-up:

DirectoryTree(origin: Directory(path: root)).remove();

Directory.create#

create() is void

Makes the directory, one level, with permissions 0755 under the umask; FileError.already_exists when it is there.

Directory.create#

create(parents is bool) is void

With parents: true, every missing directory on the way is made too, and a directory that is already there is no failure (as mkdir -p).

Directory.remove#

remove() is void

Removes the directory when it is empty; FileError.not_empty otherwise. DirectoryTree removes a whole tree.

Directory.move#

move(destination is Path) is void

Refuses a destination that already exists unless overwrite is true; an overwriting move replaces an empty directory there.

Directory.move#

Moves the directory, replacing an existing destination when overwrite is true.
